reason: post-review rework of FORGE-BOARD-7 before PR 63 merges: fix Codex findings — bytecode read-only violation, roadmap-shape robustness, doctor repo threading, skill target safety, advisory exit-code, correct an inaccurate review claim, add regression tests

quality.summary: Reviewed the FORGE-BOARD-7 post-review rework (lite window Q-0042): forge.py sets sys.dont_write_bytecode before local imports so forge sanitise --check writes no .pyc; sanitise._roadmap_drift now guards non-dict roots and non-list items and the project_gaps except widened to TypeError/AttributeError/KeyError; the [doctor-report] dump is gated on doctor_failed so --check does not print advisories then exit 0; doctor._github_slug inlines the git remote lookup with cwd=repo so branch-protection targets the --repo checkout; the sanitise skill runs cd "$TARGET" before the destructive intake --discard-active. Changes are minimal, behaviour-preserving where claimed, and each is covered: 4 new regression tests plus the existing suite, 481 passed. No over-engineering, no speculative abstraction.

performance.summary: The rework has no hot-path or algorithmic impact. sys.dont_write_bytecode only skips .pyc caching (a negligible one-time import cost on repeated runs, and the correct trade for a read-only command). The doctor slug lookup is one inlined git subprocess (same cost as the run_quiet it replaced). The roadmap-shape guards are O(1) type checks. No new I/O, fanout, or memory churn.

security.summary: The rework is net safety-positive. The skill now runs cd "$TARGET" before the destructive intake --discard-active, closing the risk of discarding task evidence in the wrong checkout. doctor._github_slug with cwd=repo stops sanitise --repo /client from reporting the current repo's branch-protection. The --check read-only contract now genuinely holds (no .pyc side effects). Malformed-roadmap input is reported rather than crashing. No secret values are printed (asserted by a new test). No new trust boundary, injection path, or unsafe default is introduced.
